rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Pili Pili Rules Summary 1.1 Goal 1.2 Bill of Materials 1.3 Gameplay Pili Pili Rules Summary Goal Pilis 🌶️ are points. Points are bad, you don't want points. The game is over when someone reaches six 🌶️. Bill of Materials The shuffled play deck is formed of: 55 numbered cards: 1 to 55, with one of each card. There are no suits. one joker card, wild in rank A shuffled mission deck is formed of 36 mission cards. Gameplay This is a once-around trick taking card game. Each hand will be determined by a mission card drawn before the cards are dealt. Each player receives the number of cards indicated on the mission card. In order each player bids, the final bidder can't make the bids even to the tricks available. Each trick is taken by the highest card played. There are no suits. a joker's value is declared when played; it can be any value 0-56. After the mission/hand/round is complete, each player receives 🌶️ for the difference between their bid and the number of tricks that took in the hand. When one player reaches 6 🌶️, the game ends and the player with the fewest 🌶️ wins.

[Rating: 2/10] Un jeu sans aucun intérêt : il reprend simplement la mécanique de jeux existants (où il fait parier sur le nombre de plis qu'on va réaliser), en enlevant toutes les possibles originalités. On se retrouve simplement avec un jeu très plat, totalement fade. Et qu'on ne me parle pas des "missions" qui rajoutent des contraintes totalement chaotiques qui brisent toute stratégie possible et enlèvent tout le "piment" (ha ha) des jeux de plis.   Rejouez plutôt à Wizard - de loin mon préféré - ou Skull King, et laissez tomber cette coquille vide qu'est Pili Pili.

[Rating: 2/10] Pili Pili is awful. Really one of the worst trick taking games I have ever played. The idea seems like it could be fun, with prediction betting and missions each round, but the game is random as hell. This is not really a trick taking game in the sense of cards of different suits. The suits on the cards don't matter and you are not required to follow suit. Only numbers on the cards matter. That's fine, there are plenty of may follow trick taking games, but the real problem is that the cards go from 1-55, so there is very little in the way to make smart predictions.
